footprint.no_data: No footprint data yet — run a deliberation to populate it.
footprint.method_body: The footprint is estimated with EcoLogits (life-cycle assessment, ISO 14044), run fully offline — no data leaves your machine. For each reply we combine the usage phase (GPU energy inferred from output tokens and latency, scaled by the data-centre PUE) with the embodied impact of manufacturing the hardware, amortised over its lifetime. Energy is converted to gCO₂e via the carbon intensity of the zone's electricity grid, and to millilitres of water via that zone's WUE (water-usage effectiveness).
footprint.title: Environmental footprint (EcoLogits)
footprint.range_aria: Estimated carbon footprint range, lower to upper bound
footprint.method_tiers: Accuracy depends on what is known about the model. Six tiers, most to least reliable: exact (registry model), alias (known equivalent), params (declared size), similar and provider-default (approximate families), then dynamic bounding — a best/worst-case physical range when the model is unknown (e.g. ':free' models with no metadata). We never show '?': always an honest range, marked '~' when it is an estimate.
footprint.method_provider_note: Anthropic and OpenAI do not publish their hardware; we use EcoLogits per-family averages. OpenRouter ':free' models often fall through to dynamic bounding for lack of metadata.
footprint.desc_declared: Model documented and verified in the EcoLogits registry.
footprint.desc_computed: Estimate calculated from the provider's declared parameter count.
footprint.desc_estimated: Projected via a similar reference model, or a conservative per-provider size class when nothing closer exists.
footprint.desc_bounded: Unknown consumption, bounded between nano (0.1 Wh) and large MoE (33 Wh).
footprint.bounding_calc_desc: With no metadata available, the footprint is bounded between two physical extremes from the literature (Jegham et al. 2025): 0.1 Wh (nano model 1-3B on H100) and 33 Wh (MoE/dense >400B on A100), scaled by output tokens and multiplied by the carbon mix of the zone.
footprint.cat_declared_long: Declared — the model (or a documented alias) is in the EcoLogits registry: architecture and size are public or well documented. The most reliable case — still a model, never a measurement.
footprint.cat_computed_long: Computed — no registry profile, but the provider declares the parameter count; the same physical model runs on that declared size. As reliable as the declaration.
footprint.cat_estimated_long: Estimated — nothing declared. We borrow the profile of a similar model of the same family, or fall back to a conservative size class for that provider. Marked '~'; the real figure can differ by a factor of a few.
footprint.cat_bounded_long: Bounded — nothing is known at all (typically ':free' community models). We refuse to invent a number: you get a physical best/worst-case interval (0.1–33 Wh per request, Jegham et al. 2025), scaled by output tokens and your grid zone.
footprint.method_assumptions:
• Energy is inferred from output tokens and request latency — we never see the GPU.
• Data-centre overhead (PUE) and water use (WUE) are sector averages, not the provider's real figures.
• Hardware manufacturing (embodied impact) is amortised over a 3-year lifetime.
• Your electricity zone applies a yearly average grid intensity — not the live mix at the moment of the request.
• Batching and serving optimisations are assumed at the methodology's defaults.
footprint.method_known: Exact token counts and latency of every call, which model and provider served it, your chosen grid zone, and — for registry models — a documented hardware and parameter profile.
footprint.method_unknown: The real GPU and data centre behind the API, the electricity mix at that very moment, the provider's true PUE/WUE, batching across customers — and the energy of input (prompt) tokens, which EcoLogits does not model yet: the true total is therefore somewhat HIGHER than shown.
